 The latest injury update for Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry on Monday night against the Phoenix Suns. Peter Dewey | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Golden State Warriors Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry has missed two of the team's first seven games this season as he manages a knee injury that he suffered in the 2025-26 season.
--> Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry has missed two of the team's first seven games this season as he manages a knee injury that he suffered in the 2025-26 season.
 Curry has played less minutes than past years (only two games where he's cracked the 30-minute threshold), and the two-time league MVP has sat out one end of a back-to-back twice in the 2026-27 campaign, including the front of end of one on Sunday against the Los Angeles Clippers.
--> Curry has played less minutes than past years (only two games where he's cracked the 30-minute threshold), and the two-time league MVP has sat out one end of a back-to-back twice in the 2026-27 campaign, including the front of end of one on Sunday against the Los Angeles Clippers.
 Despite that, ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that Curry should be clear to face the Phoenix Suns on Monday after both he and Draymond Green sat out last night's win. 
--> Despite that, ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that Curry should be clear to face the Phoenix Suns on Monday after both he and Draymond Green sat out last night's win. 
 Steph Curry and Draymond Green will both rest tomorrow night on the front side of a back-to-back against the Clippers. Injury management. That should clear them to face the Suns on Monday night.
Al Horford will play vs Clippers, meaning he would rest vs Suns.
— Anthony Slater (@anthonyVslater) October 31, 2026 That's great news for the Warriors, who have won four games in a row and are looking to stay in the palyoff hunt in the Western Conference.
